- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (e.g., 30-day forecasts often start above true values).
- Forecasts show a strong upward bias after sharp price spikes (e.g., post-49.30 or 51.55, model continues rising while true price corrects downward).
- Model fails to capture mean reversion in the short term — after a spike, forecasts remain elevated while true values revert toward prior levels.
- Forecasts tend to lag behind true price movements, particularly in the first 5–10 days of the forecast horizon.
- Model exhibits overconfidence in upward trends, especially when history shows volatility or downward corrections.
- Forecasts often overshoot the true value in the final 5–10 days of the horizon, suggesting a failure to account for near-term volatility or policy shocks.
- Model underestimates downward corrections after spikes, especially when true values drop sharply (e.g., 51.55 → 39.46 or 49.30 → 37.27).
